headline: Dry, quiet weather holds through Saturday, then a coastal storm brings a soaking rain and some wind to New York City and the region Sunday into Monday, with a low-end flooding risk; another rainy coastal storm is possible around Thanksgiving but is highly uncertain.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: High pressure keeps Friday dry and quiet across New York City and the surrounding area, with only a low chance of patchy shallow fog in outlying suburbs early this morning. Winds stay light from the west-southwest at under 10 mph today. Tonight remains dry, with winds turning light from the north or northwest and becoming nearly calm in outlying areas.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday stays dry. A coastal low-pressure system arrives Sunday, with rain developing during the day and the low passing through or just east of the area Sunday night into Monday. The air will be very moist, but the storm moves north quickly (around 23 mph), which limits how long the heavy rain lasts; the area is under a low-end (level 1 of 4) risk of flooding rain, and forecasters have added the potential for flooding late Sunday into Monday to their hazard outlook. Recent trends point to slightly less rain and less wind than earlier forecasts; rain continues early Monday with improvement possible in the afternoon and northwest gusts of 25–30 mph, and Tuesday turns dry with weakening northwest winds.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Another coastal storm could bring rain around Thanksgiving (Thursday), but the computer models disagree sharply on its track, from over Cape Cod to well south of the area. The blended forecast puts rain chances around 60% for the event, mostly as rain, though some mixed precipitation is possible inland at the start. If it materializes, it looks like another wind-and-rain event.

coast: Winds and seas stay below small-craft levels through Saturday. Seas on the ocean could build to 5 feet or more by the end of Sunday, and small-craft-advisory or even gale-force winds are possible on all waters Monday depending on the storm's track and strength; northwest winds behind the storm will likely reach small-craft levels Tuesday, especially on the ocean. With the full moon on Tuesday, minor coastal flooding is possible: the storm's coastal track would push water onshore, but weaker winds may offset that, and most guidance shows little or no flooding except in the most vulnerable back-bay spots. The extreme high end of guidance shows moderate flooding at Freeport, but that is not what most guidance suggests.
watch_for: The exact track and strength of the Sunday–Monday storm, which could still shift rain totals and flooding risk.
Minor flooding in vulnerable back-bay areas around Monday's high tides near the full moon.
Whether a second coastal storm brings rain and wind around Thanksgiving.
confidence: Confidence has increased in a rainstorm Sunday night into Monday now that models agree, though only for one run so the track and intensity could still change; confidence in the Thanksgiving storm is very low.
